data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Chemical agents, peels & baths_

**Class:** Injectable soft-tissue fillers — temporary (hyaluronic acid, collagen), semi-permanent/biostimulatory (calcium hydroxylapatite, poly-L-lactic acid), permanent (PMMA, silicone)

## Mechanism of action
- Hyaluronic acid (cross-linked, non-animal stabilised): fills volume and binds water; reversible with hyaluronidase
- Biostimulators (PLLA, CaHA): stimulate neocollagenesis over months

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Nasolabial folds, lips, cheeks/midface volume loss, tear trough, chin and jawline contouring, acne scars (rolling), HIV facial lipoatrophy (PLLA — approved)

## Dose & formulations
- Volume per region (0.5–2 mL typical); duration: HA 6–18 months, CaHA 12–18 months, PLLA ~2 years

## Adverse effects
- Bruising, swelling, lumps/nodules, Tyndall effect (blue hue — superficial HA), infection, biofilm, delayed hypersensitivity nodules
- Vascular occlusion (most serious): skin necrosis (glabella, nasal tip) and blindness (retinal artery embolism) — emergency high-dose hyaluronidase

## Contraindications
- Active infection at site, autoimmune flare, pregnancy, allergy to components (lidocaine), unrealistic expectations

## Pregnancy & lactation
Avoid.

## Viva points
- Hyaluronidase dissolves HA fillers — key in vascular occlusion
- Danger zones: glabella, nose, nasolabial (angular artery)
- Tyndall effect = superficial HA

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.59 (Injectable dermal and subcutaneous fillers); Khopkar ch.34 (Dermal fillers). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
